data.selected_experiment: Table I, (6, 6) 52-week high strategy: equally weighted winner (top 30%) minus loser (bottom 30%) portfolios ranked on the ratio of current price to the 52-week high, held 6 months, July 1963 to December 2001

economic_rationale.value: Anchoring: traders use the 52-week high as a reference point; when good news pushes a price near the 52-week high they are reluctant to bid it higher, and when bad news pushes it far from the high they are reluctant to sell as low as the information implies, so prices underreact and later continue.

evidence.quote:
traders
use the 52-week high as a reference point against which they evaluate the
potential impact of news.

universe_and_filters.value: All stocks on CRSP, 1963 to 2001, data collected exactly as described in Moskowitz and Grinblatt (1999); no further filters stated

evidence.quote:

from 1963 to 2001.

favored_group.value: 52-week high winners: top 30% of stocks with price closest to the 52-week high (highest ratio of current price to 52-week high)
